slots.name: The two halves
slots.definition: Author's rule (2026-10-14): kinetic does the work, potential fills the space. Kinetic = the writing of the information (informational pressure), which drives expansion and needs new room to keep the balance; potential = what goes into the fabric and fills it. The two are equal (the virial half). Both halves exist only AFTER the write (author, 2026-10-14): nothing is paid before the Landauer crossing, and every bit written splits its cost equally between potential (stored, filling the surface) and kinetic (the work), however many zeros are written.

cosmos.native: geometric (potential) and informational (kinetic) halves
cosmos.formula: potential half: into the fabric of spacetime, filling 'empty' space (S_geo; detected as dark matter). Kinetic half: the writing of the records, the Landauer cost on the horizon (S_info), informational pressure driving expansion (the book's dark energy with the vacuum baseline)
cosmos.source: p7_05b sec:vp_partition; p2_02 sec:vc_coupling; p4_14 sec:qr_virial

qubits.native: the two halves of each decoherence write (author, 2026-10-14)
qubits.formula: before decoherence there is no record and no half is paid; the superposition is not a half. At decoherence the qubit writes its outcome onto the substrate ('the environment acquiring records', p3_07, after Zurek 2003), and that bit's cost splits equally: potential, held in the substrate record; kinetic, the work (heat). What is written is binary, at most one bit per qubit (Holevo bound), in the pointer basis the coupling sets, copied redundantly

slots.name: Virial partition (one half at every scale)
slots.definition: IAM's Law at the boundary of every 1/r bound state: 2<K> + <V> = 0, <K> = |<V>|/2. It holds for gravity and for the Coulomb binding of every atom, molecule and bond, so it applies inside qubits, chips and cells as well as the cosmos. The virial theorem (Clausius 1870) is its mechanical special case.

_source_rule: The book (docs/book) is the source; the author's papers are only a guide to find the section. Every entry cites a book section or App. E number.
preamble: **The virial part of IAM's Law.** The book's thermodynamic identity, <K> = Q = T dS = E_Landauer, "is IAM's Law at the boundary of a bound state; the virial theorem is its mechanical special case" (Ch. What the kinetic half is, p1_04, tagged \interp). The one half it fixes holds for every 1/r binding: gravity and the Coulomb binding of every atom, molecule and bond. It therefore applies to the electrons and molecules in qubits, chips and cells, not only to the cosmos (Ch. One half at every scale, p1_03, \derived). The evidence, none of it produced by us: Hartree-Fock tables for 20 atoms and 10 molecules (Clementi & Roetti 1974; Bunge et al. 1993), the Sun and the Chandrasekhar limit, Zwicky's Coma cluster, six independent N-body simulation groups (Bryan & Norman 1998; Bett 2007; Neto 2007; Ludlow 2010; Power 2012; Klypin 2016), and the Smarr relation for black holes (Smarr 1973; Bardeen, Carter & Hawking 1973). What is still open in each domain is not whether the half holds, but which process carries which half (the 'two halves' row).
_mixed_rule: Where the book gives one entry more than one status tag, the box takes the weakest and is listed for review against the book by hand.
